full_judgment: 8. The appellate Court disbelieved the compromise decree mainly on the ground that fraud was apparent on the face of the record because the defendants appeared and filed the compromise petition before the summons was issued and served, and that Kanailal Dhar was not authorized to act on behalf of all the defendants. The High Court, Division after giving good reasons, upheld the compromise decree. It was held that under sub-rule (1) of rule 1 of Order 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure the defendants could appear at the presentation of the plaint and admit the plaintiffs' claim and there was no necessity for issuing any summons upon the defendants. It was further found that Kanailal Dhar acted on behalf of all the defendants and that defendant No. 5 after obtaining the compromise decree filed a mutation case under section 54 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and got her name recorded.
